output.subject: We've received your complaint about your online banking
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for contacting us. We have received your complaint, and we understand how alarming and stressful this situation must be.

You told us that on Sunday, September 6, you received an email saying the email address on your online banking had been changed, and that you did not make that change. You mentioned that by the time you reached us, $7,925.50 had been transferred out to an account you do not recognize. You also told us you believe whoever did this got past the security questions using your personal information.

You said you are now locked out of online banking, and that no one has been able to tell you when your access will be restored or when you will get your money back. You have asked us to restore your access, return the funds, and respond to you this week.

A specialist team is reviewing your complaint and will respond within 10 business days. We are sorry for the worry and frustration this has caused, and we appreciate you taking the time to tell us what happened.

Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: Customer reports an account takeover with $7,925.50 transferred out. Confirm the case is with Fraud & Disputes and that any fraud claim or recall has been opened.
Customer asked for a response this week, but the draft gives only the 10 business day timeframe. Decide whether to contact them sooner, for example by phone.
Customer says they are locked out. Check whether access can be restored securely and whether to say so in the reply.
Customer asked for a refund of the stolen funds. The draft only acknowledges this request and does not commit to an outcome.
Customer believes their SSN was compromised. Consider whether to add guidance on identity protection.
Consider adding security advice, such as warning about phishing contacts that claim to be from the bank, since the email channel may be compromised.
Confirm that the reply goes to a verified contact address, because the customer reports their email on file was changed by someone else.
Customer says they will move their accounts to a credit union if they don't hear back this week. This is a retention risk.
